newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-DAYLAMI, ALWAYS LOYAL WIN FRENCH CLASSICS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DAYLAMI, ALWAYS LOYAL WIN FRENCH CLASSICS.

text.p: Daylami, owned by the Aga Khan and
ridden by Gerald Mosse, ran out a convincing winner of the Poule
d'Essai des Poulaine (French 2,000 Guineas) for three-year-old
colts run over one mile (1.6 km) at Longchamp on Sunday.
Mosse held the colt at the back of the six-runner field, but
the grey powered up the outside on the rain-sodden turf to take
the lead inside the final 150 metres and pull two lengths clear
of second placed Loup Sauvage, the mount of Olivier Peslier.
Visionary, ridden by Thierry Jarnet, was a further 2-1/2
lengths back in the field of six.
The British trained trio of Yalaientanee, Bahamian Bounty
and Fantastic Fellow filled the last three places.
It was a repeat performance for the Aga Khan-Gerald Mosse
and trainer Alain de Royer-Duprem combination, successful last
year with Ashkalani.
Royer-Dupre said: "I have always had tremendous confidence
in the colt. He is a pure miler that acts on any going.
"The only time he has been beaten is when we tried him over
longer distances. He will probably now try and avenge
Ashkalani's defeat in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal
Ascot in June."
Earlier, Madame Criquette Head trained her sixth Poule
d'Essai des Pouliches (French 1,000 Guineas) winner when Always
Loyal, the mount of Freddie Head, came home a head winner from
the Cash Asmussen ridden Seebe.
Red Camellia, who made most of the running in the one mile
race, was a further 3/4 of a length back in third place in the
seven-runner field.
The winner, who was maintaining her 100 percent record, is
owned by Maktoum Al Maktoum.
Criquette Head said: "Always Loyal is a very couragoues
filly that should stay longer. Her next target may be the Prix
de Diane or Coronation Stakes."
